messages:
maya: Quick check — onboarding chatlet-v2 weights (s3 path below). Seeing weird token deltas when we prepend the system prompt: sometimes an extra sentinel appears between system and user. Anyone else run into this?

arjun: Which weights path and tokenizer artifact are you using?

maya: s3://rw-models/chatlet-v2/weights/2026-03-15 and tokenizer at s3://rw-models/chatlet-v2/tokenizer/tokenizer.json. Repro steps: locally encode 'System: <start>You are a helpful assistant\nUser: Hi' and compare tokens vs model runtime.

lisa: That path rings a bell — we changed sentinel mapping in the last upload. The tokenizer.json in that bucket still has the old sentinel table (start/stop mapped to multi-byte sequences). Could be a mismatch with the chat template that expects single byte sentinels.

sasha: Short reproduce command I used: 
```
python -c "from tokenizers import Tokenizer; t=Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizer.json'); print(t.encode('System: <start>Hello\nUser: Hi').tokens)"
```
On the old tokenizer that prints: ['System', ':', '<start>', 'Hello', '\\n', 'User', ':', 'Hi'] but on the updated model runtime it shows an extra '<sep>' token between '<start>' and 'Hello'.

arjun: Hmm. Do we have config validation on model load that checks special token ids (bos/eos/start/stop) vs chat template expectations? If not, we should fail fast.

lisa: Currently we validate vocab size + model dtype + quantization bits. Special tokens got missed. I can add a quick check: assert tokenizer.special_tokens['start'] in expected_set and likewise for 'stop' and 'sep'. If mismatch -> log and abort onboarding.

tom: I pushed a tiny PR that adds a preflight check and a unit test for the chat template token sequence. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/models/pull/789 — includes test data and a small re-mapping utility (`tools/remap_sentinels.py`).

maya: Nice. Can you also include the exact token id mapping we expect? For reference: start -> 50256, stop -> 50257, sep -> 50258 in our serving profiles for chatlet series.

tom: Yep added to the PR description and test asserts. Also added a migration script that rewrites tokenizer.json sentinel entries if we detect multi-byte sequences to canonical ids.

sasha: One thing to watch: our prefix caching logic expects the prefix tokens to be byte-for-byte identical between client and server. If remap happens at runtime but cached prefixes were encoded with the old mapping, you'll see off-by-one tokens in cache hits. Need a cache invalidation step when tokenizer mapping changes.

lisa: Good catch. I'll add a cache-flush trigger to the onboarding pipeline whenever sentinel mapping differs from last-deployed. That will be a soft TTL + explicit flush on deploy for the first rollout.

arjun: Ops/playback question — where should the canonical tokenizer artifact live? We should not rely on multiple copies in weights buckets. Propose: promote tokenizer.json to gs://redwood-artifacts/tokenizers/chatlet-v2/<sha>/tokenizer.json and have weights reference that SHA in manifest.

maya: Agreed. For now I'll pin the weights manifest to the tokenizer SHA and rerun the onboarding after Tom's PR lands.

deploy-bot: Deploy check queued for PR #789. CI: unit tests 12/12 passing, lints green.

maya: Action items: (1) Tom merge PR -> adds preflight + remap tool, (2) Lisa add cache-flush/validation in pipeline, (3) Arjun update manifest to point canonical tokenizer SHA location, (4) I'll re-run onboarding and flag any runtime diffs.

sasha: Also add a short regression eval for a handful of prompts to verify no extra separator tokens after merge. Put eval cases in tests/regression/chatlet_sentinels.json.

maya: Thanks all — ping me @channel when PR is merged and the new tokenizer is promoted. :thumbsup:
